'''''Dalbergia odorifera''''', '''fragrant rosewood''' or '''Chinese rosewood''',<ref name="ars">{{GRIN | accessdate = 21 January 2018}}</ref> is a species of [[Rosewood|true rosewood]] in the genus [[Dalbergia]]. It is a small or medium-sized tree, {{convert|10|-|15|m}} tall.<ref name="eflora">{{cite web|url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=242316792|title=''Dalbergia odorifera''|author=Dezhao Chen|author2=Dianxiang Zhang|author3=Kai Larsen|name-list-style=amp|work=Flora of China|publisher=Missouri Botanical Garden, St. Louis, MO & Harvard University Herbaria, Cambridge, MA|access-date=18 May 2012}}</ref> It is endemic to China and occurs in [[Fujian]], [[Hainan]], [[Zhejiang]],<ref name=eflora/> and [[Guangdong]].<ref name="Furniture">{{cite web|url=http://www.eastcornercompany.com/doc/The%20best%20Chinese%20furniture%20woods.pdf|title=The best Chinese furniture woods|publisher=eastcornercompany.com|access-date=2011-08-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303180150/http://www.eastcornercompany.com/doc/The%20best%20Chinese%20furniture%20woods.pdf|archive-date=2016-03-03}}</ref>

== Description ==
A deciduous tree, ''D. odorifera'' will start shedding leaves at around December of each year in the Northern Hemisphere. It becomes dormant throughout the winter months.

== Threats ==
It was [[overexploitation|overexploited]] in the twentieth century and was classed as a [[vulnerable species]] in 1998.<ref name="iucn status 14 November 2021" /> This reached a level in the early twenty-first century where most trees of a size for commercial use had been cut down. As a consequence, other species of ''Dalbergia'' started to be exploited in its place.<ref name="Barstow_et_al_2022">{{cite web |title=Siamese Rosewood Dalbergia cochinchinensis |url=https://www.iucnredlist.org/species/215342548/2822125 |access-date=22 July 2022 |website=ICUN Red List}}</ref>

== Uses ==
It is used as a wood product and in folk medicine.<ref name="ars" /> This valuable wood was used in [[Chinese furniture]] from the late [[Ming Dynasty|Ming]] and early [[Qing Dynasty|Qing]] dynasties,<ref name="Furniture" /> and new furniture in the same styles are sought after as luxury and prestige items.<ref name="Barstow_et_al_2022" />
[[Image:WLA haa Dressing Cabinet Qing Huanghuali wood.jpg|thumb|left|220px|Chinese dressing cabinet made from Huanghuali wood, Qing Dynasty (17th-18th century)]]

Four compounds isolated from the root of this plant have been shown in a laboratory to have [[antioxidant]] properties.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Yu |first1=X. |last2=Wang |first2=W. |last3=Yang |first3=M. |year=2007 |title=Antioxidant activities of compounds isolated from ''Dalbergia odorifera'' T. Chen and their inhibition effects on the decrease of glutathione level of rat lens induced by UV irradiation |journal=Food Chemistry |volume=104 |issue=2 |pages=715–720 |doi=10.1016/j.foodchem.2006.10.081}}</ref>
